title: Universal Knowledge Graph Database — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Linked entities, concepts, evidence, relationships, and domain-specific ontologies in one graph. The Universal Knowledge Graph Database stores knowledge as a graph: entities (people, places, concepts, things) linked by typed relationships, with evidence attached to every edge. Instead of isolated documents, facts live in a web where 'Marie Curie — discovered — radium — evidenced by — 1911 Nobel citation' is one traversable structure. Records include entity schemas, relationship ontologies, evidence-attachment rules, and query patterns that turn the graph into answers.

title: Universal Knowledge Graph Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Graph model: triples (subject, predicate, object) plus edge metadata (sources[], confidence in [0,1], valid_from/valid_to). Ontology: classes (Person, Discovery, Award), subclass relations, property domains/ranges, cardinality constraints. Identity: entities get canonical IDs; aliases merge via the identity-resolution rules. Query patterns: 1-hop (entity facts), 2-hop (entity->relation->entity->relation->entity), path queries with evidence aggregation (combined confidence = product of edge confidences along the path, reported as a range). Reasoning: subclass inheritance (a Physicist is a Scientist), inverse relations (discovered-by inverts discovered). Quality: orphan entities (no edges) and evidence-free edges are flagged by the integrity checker.

title: Universal Knowledge Graph Database — Execution: runnable tool
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Demos execute triple loading, a 2-hop evidence-graded query, integrity checking on a flawed graph, and a merge of two overlapping graphs.

demo.title: Execution: identity resolution matching
demo.code: function jw(a,b){a=a.toLowerCase();b=b.toLowerCase();if(a===b)return 1;let m=0;const n=Math.min(a.length,b.length);for(let i=0;i<n;i++)if(a[i]===b[i])m++;return m/Math.max(a.length,b.length);}const pairs=[['Jon Smith','John Smith'],['Jon Smith','Maria Garcia']];const scored=pairs.map(([x,y])=>({x,y,s:+jw(x,y).toFixed(2)}));J({scored});assert(scored[0].s>scored[1].s,'match');

title: Universal Knowledge Graph Database — Verification: tests and limitations
body: Public edition. Sourced public knowledge, fact-checked reference; never mixed with Signature records. Tests: ontology-conformance test (every triple's predicate fits its domain/range); evidence test (no edge claims confidence without a source); query test (known answers returned with correct evidence chains); merge test (duplicate entities merge, distinct ones do not); determinism test. Limitations: confidence combination is heuristic; ontology design is human judgment; the in-memory engine is for testing, not production scale. Every ontology carries a version and changelog.

demo.title: Execution: pipeline stage hashing and replay
demo.code: const crypto=require('crypto');function h(s){return crypto.createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex').slice(0,8);}const stages=['import','clean','validate','export'];const data='raw-data-v1';let cur=data;const hashes=stages.map(s=>{cur=s+':'+cur;return s+'='+h(cur);});const replay=(()=>{let c=data;return stages.map(s=>{c=s+':'+c;return s+'='+h(c);});})();J({hashes:hashes.length,replayMatch:JSON.stringify(hashes)===JSON.stringify(replay)});assert(JSON.stringify(hashes)===JSON.stringify(replay),'replay');
